plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Gnarled branches that still look like winter are covered in blossoms. The five-petaled, round-edged flowers give off a sweet, spicy fragrance that drifts through shrine gardens and orchards. Ume are among the first trees to bloom, and they often flower while cold air is still around.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to March, with late-season trees and cultivars still in full flower in early March
plants.location: Japan, including plum groves and shrine gardens across Honshu. It is also widely grown in China and Korea.
plants.funFact: Ume blooms weeks before cherry blossoms, so in East Asian art and poetry it is a symbol of perseverance and the first hint of spring. Its fruit is pickled as umeboshi and steeped into plum liqueur.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: This Himalayan forest giant covers its bare branches in huge, goblet-shaped blooms before any leaves appear. Pink to rose petals open wide like pale lanterns above the mountain slopes, and the flowers have dark purple-red stamens at the centre.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (roughly February or March to May, depending on altitude and the year)
plants.location: Eastern Himalaya, including Nepal, Sikkim, Bhutan and Assam, plus parts of Tibet and Yunnan. It is also grown in mild-climate gardens elsewhere.
plants.funFact: A seedling can take 20 years or more to bloom for the first time. The wait is why mature trees in flower are such a prized sight.
